correctness.rationale: For an admissible center the quotient gives distinct supporting directions and on each line the Q points have monic equation sigma^Q−sigma+beta^Q−beta. A degree-Q equation of a reduced (Q,Q+1) complete intersection cannot contain a support line: the other equation would meet it in length Q+1 rather than Q. Its common leading coefficient at the vertex is nonzero, so its sigma coefficient gives precisely the degree-(Q−1) interpolation condition. Conversely degree-Q interpolation supplies the constants independently, and intersecting the resulting curve with the union of the support lines gives the desired reduced scheme. In a quotient basis normalized by the volume form det(u,−,−), Vandermonde cofactors give the stated homogeneous polynomial of degree Q(Q−1)/2; at u=v_i only the i-th cofactor survives. On an external rational line h(u)=0, h descends and h^(Q−1) interpolates all ones. Frobenius orbits of size two on the nonrational elements of F_(Q^2) give exactly Q(Q−1)/2 monic irreducible quadratics, exhausting the degree and proving reducedness. Counting tangent and secant incidences is valid in both characteristics: off the conic, odd Q has zero or two tangents, while even Q has one except at the nucleus, where all tangents meet. Every rational point of an external line is therefore on a secant; all intersections with rational secants or other external lines are rational. The good direction components are disjoint punctured projective lines, and a rational puncture chosen at infinity trivializes the affine-line fiber of centers. This gives the exact point count and zeta function. For Q=2 the independent calculation gives U+V+W as the only factor, with three rational points on that external line, consistent with the characteristic-two case.
residual_risks: The package's checks for six orders are recorded supplementary evidence, not independent reruns or proof for all Q. The geometric argument does not describe forbidden centers or a full Weddle scheme.

value.rationale: The generic dichotomy leaves open whether good exceptional centers exist and, if so, where they are defined. Here one gets an explicit reduced divisor and a complete description on its natural open set, including the absence of base-field centers despite existence over every proper finite extension. This is a structural computation of a motivated projection locus in positive characteristic, not just a finite conic-incidence count.
residual_risks: Value is for this symmetric conic family and the admissible locus only; it is not a general Weddle classification.
